correctness.rationale: For any finite A⊂Z, Parseval turns the fourth power L⁴ norm into n²+2Σ_{h>0}|C_h|². The diagonal of E=Σ|C_h|² is binomial(n,2); independent Haar characters make every off-diagonal term mean zero. For positive h and distinct correlation start points x<y, let d=y−x. The exponent vector is (+ at x+h and x+d; − at x and x+d+h). If d=h it is the unique 3-term progression character (−1,2,−1) and its conjugate; each counts 2 in Var(E). If d≠h it is a four-distinct equal-sum character, and (d,h) versus (h,d) are its only two occurrences; the conjugate pair contributes 8 in Var(E). Thus Var(X)=4(2T+8Q)=8T+32Q; every nontrivial B₂ collision in integer support is of one of these two forms. Independently enumerated exponent vectors for all 255 nonempty subsets of {0,…,7}, comparing coefficients exactly with T,Q, not as replacement for the proof. Conjugates are distinct and no torsion occurs on Z.
residual_risks: Requires independent Haar unit phases; finite cyclic groups or non-Haar coefficients have different collision structures.
No distribution of X beyond its first two moments is claimed.
